generator: slots are independent (a larger spec reproduces every slot of the smaller one byte for byte, apart from cross-instance action-uniqueness redraws)
serialisation round trip (tuples restored; re-serialised sha identical)
vstep == env.step on 20,000 random transitions (any status)

primary dev set file (dev2_primary.jsonl): sha256 == SOURCE record == regenerated in memory from (seed, recorded spec) + the recorded freshness rejections (0), without loading the exclusion union; generator lbeam-problems-v2; spec == the registered primary_spec()

oor dev set file (dev2_oor.jsonl): sha256 == SOURCE record == regenerated in memory from (seed, recorded spec) + the recorded freshness rejections (0), without loading the exclusion union; generator lbeam-problems-v2; spec == the registered oor_spec()

PRIMARY set: every instance re-verifies (BFS d*, plans, fixed candidates, oracle, in-range definition, reachable-state closure incl. the rule-blind dynamics, no void step on an optimal plan); only 'in' instances; n = 120 (24 per d* = 2..6)
DESCRIPTIVE oor set: re-verifies; only 'oor' instances, drawn as a separate set with its own seed (never pooled with the primary); n = 30 (6 per d*)

closure, re-derived independently (env.step on dicts, not the generator's vstep): for EVERY primary instance, every state reachable from init by any sequence of <= 8 vocabulary actions has |b| <= 98; the reachable-state counts equal the generator's records

every vocabulary action of the primary set lies in T2's trained surface: amount one of the 21 trained values (-9..12, so |amount| <= 12), status posted / void, accounts A-D (sorted canonical state), kinds add / scale / transfer

the closure covers the rule-blind dynamics: applying every void twin as posted (IGNORE_STATUS; OFF's dominant error) reaches exactly the same state set on every primary instance (each twin repeats a posted vocabulary action's arithmetic)
the generator enforces the closure (draws rejected for it while building the primary set); the superseded v1 dev set (no closure) fails it on most of its 'in' instances
descriptive oor set: every instance leaves T2's verified range (an untrained amount in its vocabulary, or a state with |b| > 98 within 8 steps)
beam_kwargs: max_depth = D_CLOSE - simulated candidate length (enum depth 1: 7; enum depth 2: 6; random L6 R3: 5; random one-shot L6: 2; fixed / oracle plans <= 6: 2); the hooks are lbeam_problems'
answer-free floors computed (primary): fixed view uniform-over-void-free > 1/K; greedy true-unmet descent solves part of the set (reported; score() splits success by greedy / needs_lookahead)
planner_instances() is blind by default: exactly id / init / goal / objs, no answer key (opt plan, seed plan, vocab roles, fixed candidates) reachable from what BWM receives
RandomProposer (no instance list needed): deterministic; batch-independent (CRN on (eval_seed, id, round, j)); eval_seed and round change the draws; n_tokens 0; plans from the item's objs
EnumerateProposer: the V = 8 single actions in vocabulary order per item; deterministic, batch- and seed-independent; n_tokens 0; depth 2 gives V^2 = 64 sequences
FixedCandidatesProposer / select_fixed take the RCWM records: the stored K candidates at round 0, nothing later; both refuse the blind planner dicts

RangeGuardF: a primary key with an input balance |b| = 99 returns None without reaching the inner F; keys outside applies_to (the descriptive oor set) pass unguarded; admitted keys go to the inner F in one predict call
plan_beam + OracleProposer + guarded ORACLE F (W1 E1): success 1.0, verified 1.0, precision 1.0, every plan of optimal length d*; nothing refused
F accounting: model_queries == distinct keys requested == sum of per-instance attributions (every action has one owner)
plan_beam + FixedCandidatesProposer + guarded ORACLE F (W1 E1): success 1.0 (the optimal candidate is found)
select_fixed + guarded ORACLE F: success 1.0, regret 0; F calls/instance <= distinct candidate prefixes <= K x d* and == the fixed view through plan_beam
select_fixed + IGNORE_STATUS F (void treated as posted): success well below 1 - the problems punish ignoring the void rule

ORACLE F through plan_beam on all 120 primary instances: success never falls as E grows (CRN / deterministic enumeration replays the smaller run); precision 1.0 everywhere; success >= 0.95 at the most generous budgets of both proposers
